objective: Make local-model HTTP responses resource-bounded and explicit about their contract, so an oversized, non-JSON, error-status, or malformed response is rejected as a bounded LocalModelError instead of being read into memory or parsed as provider content.
acceptance: a declared Content-Length above the response cap is refused before the body is read
a body without Content-Length is refused while reading, so the cap holds for chunked responses too
a malformed or negative Content-Length header is reported as a bounded LocalModelError
non-2xx HTTP status is reported by status code without echoing the response body
a missing or non-JSON Content-Type is rejected before JSON parsing is attempted
a truncated or malformed JSON body fails with a stable message rather than leaking the exception text of the parser
last_call telemetry is only recorded for a fully accepted route, so a rejected response cannot leave partial provider content behind
the loopback and allow-list endpoint policy from the existing implementation is unchanged
every new boundary is covered by a test that fails when the corresponding guard is removed
evidence: focused boundary test output for oversized declared, oversized streamed, non-JSON, missing Content-Type, error status, truncated JSON, and malformed Content-Length responses
demonstration that the focused boundary tests fail against the previous implementation and pass against the fix
confirmation that the five pre-existing local-model tests still pass unchanged
full repository test and Task Packet gate output
stop_conditions: the fix requires a new third-party HTTP client or JSON dependency
the response cap must be configurable per caller, which is a policy decision rather than a boundary fix
an interfaces schema or libs/contracts change is required
a modification outside allowed_paths is required
